members.reason: ["Committee-creation condition (item 1: 'a Lace Manufacturing Industry Committee be created to cooperate with the Administrator as a Planning and Fair Practice Agency', with five elected representatives and three members without vote appointed by the Administrator) is a separate command beside the code approval. No held record shows when or whether the committee was created or when it ended. EO 6539 recites 'An application having been duly made by the Lace Manufacturing Industry Committee under date of September 27, 1933', which shows only that a committee of that name existed by September 27, 1933. That the repeal of the code-approval power ended the committee's existence or the Administrator's appointment power is not shown by any held source and is not assumed. Needed: a held record of the committee's creation and dissolution, or a reviewed rule on whether such a condition falls with the approval.", "The held text is internally inconsistent about the amended code's submission date: the recital says an amended code was submitted 'on August 7, 1933' and the operative sentence says 'as amended and submitted on July 7, 1933'. The date is not material to the end but should be checked against an official copy."]

["Condition (1) directs a private association: 'The National Lime Association shall, as soon as practicable, amend its bylaws' by repealing a membership-nomination provision. 'As soon as practicable' states no date, no held record shows whether or when the National Lime Association amended its bylaws, and the command is not shown to depend on the code approval in a way that the repeal of section 3 would end. Under the owner's 2026-10-28 ruling an interval is claimed only when evidence shows the event happened in it, and a repeal date is an end only with a reason it extinguished the command. Needed: a held record of the bylaw amendment (or its absence) or a reviewed rule on conditions of approval."]

["Code Authority condition (item 1: 'a Marking Devices Industry Code Authority be created to cooperate with the Administrator as a Planning and Fair Practice Agency', with eleven elected representatives and three members without vote appointed by the Administrator) is a separate command beside the code approval. No held record shows when or whether the authority was created or when it ended; no other held text names the authority. The held text also calls the body both a 'Code Authority' and a 'committee' in the same sentence. That the repeal of the code-approval power ended the authority or the appointment power is not shown by any held source and is not assumed. Needed: a held record of the authority's creation and dissolution, or a reviewed rule on whether such a condition falls with the approval."]

["Mixed order. Condition 2 creates an Inter-Code Committee ('an Inter-Code committee of seven (7) persons shall be appointed by the Administrator'), authorizes it to administer and supervise enforcement and issue interpretations, and directs: 'On or before June 30, 1934, the Inter-Code Committee shall report to the two Code Authorities concerned, and to the Administrator'. A report date is a deadline, not an end; no held record shows whether or when the committee was appointed or reported, or when it ended, and the committee's end is not established by the repeal of the code-approval power. The order also directs the Administrator to arrange with the two Code Authorities an equitable basis of contribution, a further command with no end. The effective-date command ('shall be modified to the foregoing effect on and after January 2, 1934') and the Cotton Garment code approval of November 17, 1933 (a different order, not in this packet) would each need their own earlier-end check. The machine inventory is also mis-segmented (duplicate scopes #1-dup2, #1-dup3, #2-dup2). Needed: a held record of the committee's appointment, report and dissolution, or a reviewed rule on these commands, and a corrected inventory."]

["Section 4(a) agreement: the Administrator found 'the agreement provided for in Article X of the said Amendments, pursuant to the provisions of subsection (a) of Section 4 of the said Act' and the amendments are approved with Article X in them. Section 4(a) agreement authority is a category the shared analysis expressly does not decide; S.J. Res. 113 section 1 extended Title I to April 1, 1936 and section 2 repealed only the code approval and enforcement provisions, so the end of an approved 4(a) agreement is not shown by the June 14, 1935 repeal. The approval is also 'subject to the following condition', which provides that 'the Administrator may, upon recommendation of the Investment Bankers Code Committee or otherwise, and after such notice and hearing as he may specify, approve such modification or amendment of this Code as amended'. That standing delegation to the Administrator is a separate command with no stated end. Needed: a reviewed rule for the section 4(a) agreement approval and for the delegated modification power, with the order's operative clauses separated."]

["Mixed order. Condition 1 grants an exemption from other codes ('is hereby granted an exemption and exception from such other Code of Fair Competition') to manufacturers who elect, and sets election periods running from the code's effective date ('shall, within forty-five (15) days from the effective date of the Code of Fair Competition for the Infants' and Children's Wear Industry, have the right to elect', where the text states both 'forty-five' and '(15)'; a second period of fifteen days runs from commencing manufacture). The effective date of the Code of Fair Competition for the Infants' and Children's Wear Industry is not held in this packet, so the periods cannot be dated and a condition running from the effective date needs that date. Condition 1 also directs: 'Each of the above mentioned associations shall forthwith submit to the Administrator certified copies of the list of their members', an independent direction to two associations with no end and no held evidence of performance. Condition 2 and condition 3 allocate manufacturers among codes and carry their own scope questions. Each command needs its own end or a block; the shared analysis ends only the code approval itself. Needed: the code's held effective date, the clause-by-clause analysis of conditions 1 to 3, and evidence or a reviewed rule for the list-submission direction."]
